simple.meaning: סְבָךְ (çᵉbâk) is a Hebrew word meaning “a copse.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: סְבָךְ (H5442) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 22:13, with occurrences in Genesis, Psalms, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סְבָךְ (H5442) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in סְבָךְ (H5442) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: סְבָךְ (çᵉbâk) / H5442 is traced through Genesis 22:13, Psalms 74:5, Isaiah 9:17, Isaiah 10:34 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and saw that behind him was a ram caught in the thicket by his horns. Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering instead of his son.
